subject: ss-critical-care
title: Extracorporeal life support: modes, cannulation and weaning

steps.tx: **EOLIA** enrolled very severe ARDS, including PaO2/FiO2 below 50 for more than 3 hours or below 80 for more than 6 hours despite optimisation. The primary 60 day mortality difference was not statistically significant, and many control patients crossed over to **ECMO**. Bayesian post-hoc analyses suggested a substantial probability of treatment benefit for early extracorporeal gas exchange.

steps.tx: **CESAR** randomised transfer to an ECMO centre, not ECMO itself. Survival without severe disability was better in the transfer arm. Not every transferred patient received ECMO. Centralising care in specialized tertiary centres with dedicated perfusion teams, structured protective ventilation protocols, and round-the-clock retrieval capabilities explains much of the demonstrated clinical advantage.

rows: Transfer to specialized centre vs local care
63% vs 47% survival without severe disability at 6 months
25% of transferred patients improved with conventional care
Early transfer to expert centres improves complex ARDS outcomes

steps.tx: **VV-ECMO** supports gas exchange and does not provide cardiac output. **VA-ECMO** bypasses the heart and lungs and does provide flow. The configuration is chosen from the failing organ. Veno-venous cannulation removes blood from a vena cava and returns oxygenated blood to the right atrium, maintaining native pulsatile pulmonary circulation.

left.title: Veno-venous (VV-ECMO)
points: Indicated for isolated refractory respiratory failure
Relies entirely on native cardiac contractility

right.title: Veno-arterial (VA-ECMO)
points: Indicated for cardiogenic shock and cardiac arrest
Provides full haemodynamic and respiratory support
Returns pressurized blood directly into arterial tree

steps.tx: **Harlequin**, or north south, syndrome on peripheral VA-ECMO occurs when the recovering heart ejects poorly oxygenated blood to the upper body while the femoral return oxygenates the legs. The **right radial arterial** gas detects and confirms it. Mixing of native desaturated blood with retrograde oxygenated perfusate occurs in the aortic arch, risking cerebral and coronary hypoxic injury.

rows: Native LV ejects desaturated blood from injured lungs
Monitor right radial arterial line and cerebral oximetry
Retrograde femoral ECMO cannula delivers oxygenated blood
V-AV hybrid cannulation or ventilator optimization
Add right internal jugular venous infusion line

steps.tx: Peripheral VA-ECMO increases **left ventricular afterload**. A distended, non-ejecting left ventricle needs a **vent**, such as an **Impella**, a septostomy, or an intra-aortic balloon. Retrograde arterial flow increases end-systolic wall stress, causing left ventricular dilation, catastrophic pulmonary oedema, intracardiac stasis, and aortic valve closure that halts coronary perfusion.

left.title: LV afterload increase
points: Retrograde femoral arterial jet impedes LV ejection
Elevates end-diastolic pressure and wall stress

right.title: Unloading modalities
points: Percutaneous balloon atrial septostomy decompresses LA
Direct surgical apical vent or intra-aortic balloon pump

steps.tx: Circuit **anticoagulation** is usually **unfractionated heparin**, monitored by **anti-Xa** or **ACT**. Bleeding, not clotting alone, is the complication that most often limits support. Continuous contact with synthetic tubing activates the contact coagulation cascade and platelets, requiring constant titration to balance intracranial haemorrhage risks against acute oxygenator membrane thrombosis.

rows: More reliable heparin monitoring than aPTT in acute illness
Rapid point-of-care test during cannulation and procedures
Reduces risk of lethal gastrointestinal and intracranial bleeding

steps.tx: The **RESP score** estimates survival on respiratory ECMO. The **SAVE score** estimates survival on cardiac ECMO. Both are **counselling** tools, not a refusal rule used alone. Scoring incorporates age, immunocompromised status, pre-cannulation mechanical ventilation duration, neurological dysfunction, and organ failure markers to assist shared clinical decision-making.

left.title: RESP prognostic score
points: Validated for acute severe hypoxaemic respiratory failure
Stratifies survival from Class I over 90% to Class V under 20%
Considers duration of mechanical ventilation prior to ECMO

right.title: SAVE prognostic score
points: Validated for refractory cardiogenic shock on VA-ECMO
Incorporate aetiology, pre-ECMO arrest, and organ failure
Guides multidisciplinary expectations and family discussions

steps.tx: **Extracorporeal carbon dioxide removal** uses low blood flow and does not oxygenate. It is not standard ARDS care. **ECPR** is VA-ECMO started during cardiac arrest, and it is limited to systems that can cannulate without a long no-flow time. Rapid establishment of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation within sixty minutes of collapse maximizes neurologically intact survival.
